The Bentley Infotainment Upgrade Keeps Second-Gen Continental GT, GTC, and Flying Spur Up to Snuff
7 photos
Photo: Bentley
The ultra-luxury British automaker is taking a page out of Porsche's Classic Communication Management Plus (PCCM Plus) book with the new update for older models. Actually, they’re not that old, since we’re talking about the Bentley Continental GT, GT Convertible, and Flying Spur models built between 2012 and 2019.
Porsche has vast experience with upgrading and updating the infotainment solutions for its older models – just recently, in late September 2026, they announced a new generation of the Porsche Classic Communication Management Plus ( PCCM Plus ) dedicated to more than 300k examples of the 911, Cayman, and Boxster models produced from model years 2009 through 2016.
Bentley, too, has a solution for the slightly older models to get all the latest goodies from 2026 - Bentley Infotainment Upgrade, available from Bentley retailers, is a swap solution that directly replaces the existing console infotainment screen and also the physical heater controls with an all-new unit. The latter has a larger and crisper screen, fast processor speeds, the latest navigation maps, and full smartphone integration.
Both Apple CarPlay and Android Auto connect with the unit via Bluetooth or a wired connection in the center console. Bentley's design team was brought in to design the new unit and features digital graphics inspired by Bentley's latest models but “preserves the elegance and sophistication of the original cabin while introducing a cleaner, more contemporary user experience that feels entirely at home within the vehicle.”
The Bentley Infotainment Upgrade has a new 9.7-inch display and integrated climate controls, making it ideal for the second-generation Continental GT, Continental GT Convertible and Flying Spur model owners who seek a “contemporary digital experience delivered with a distinctly Bentley approach.” The new touchscreen has 2K resolution, but on the other hand it includes most of the climate settings in a touch-controlled manner, instead of full physical controls.
The infotainment upgrade comes with improved DAB+, FM, AM and SXM (US only) tuning, and the integrated navigation system has the latest map data along with immersive 3D presentation. Map data can be updated, and the enhanced graphics are doubled with integrated speed limit information.
The Bentley Infotainment Upgrade “brings modern connectivity and enhanced usability to some of Bentley's most admired grand tourers, (…) it enables owners to enjoy the latest digital technology while preserving the craftsmanship, refinement and sense of occasion that define a Bentley.”
As for Bentley’s novelties, there have been a handful in recent times, like the Olympia Collection by Mulliner , which celebrates the spirit of W.O. Bentley through an exclusive Mulliner collection of 12 individually curated and numbered Continental GTs inspired by the journey that led to the creation of the legendary Bentley 6 ½ Liter shown a century ago at the 1926 Olympia Motor Show.
The company also presented its all-new Torcal in New York City last month, marking the arrival of the marque's first fully electric model, with help from a Flying Spur Art Car by Death Spray Custom, both celebrating their premiere at CART Department in New York City.
Last but not least, the brand recently named acclaimed actor and producer Michelle Yeoh as its latest global brand ambassador. They also like to cover just about everything else, from hosting an annual global brand ambassador to celebrate its Crewe community to announcing the latest perfume from Bentley Fragrances, named Become Odyssey!

Polestar Formula 2030 Concept Breaks Cover, Looks Futuristic in the Healthiest Way Possible
54 photos
Photo: Polestar
What you see is what you're going to get with the new Formula 2030 concept car from Polestar. Meaning, future models from the Swedish brand will be inspired by what we're seeing here today, and we've already received confirmation that among those models will be the upcoming Polestar 7 and the next-generation Polestar 2.
Just when you thought things couldn't get more futuristic than the Polestar 5, here comes this concept with a roof height of just 1,350 mm (53.1 in) - even lower than that of the previously mentioned model. The Formula 2030 concept also happens to be 4.68 meters (184 in) long, about 2 meters (78.7 in) wide, and has a 2.78 meter-long (109.4 in) wheelbase. It's a somewhat compact four-door "sports car", according to Polestar. Yes, they used the term sports car, not us.
To me, it looks more like a compact four-door GT car. A smaller and more neatly packaged version of the ridiculously expensive Polestar 5 . By the way, could this be the body style of the future on all non-SUV models? There's a good chance that it will be, because the traditional three-box sedan shape isn't the most practical. Feel free to travel around western Europe, especially in Italy and Spain, and you'll notice how hatchbacks and wagons outnumber sedans by the millions.
The side profile tells you everything you need to know with that classic cab rearward stance extending into those powerful rear haunches. Then you've got the long hood, short overhands, the 22" wheels, coke bottle hips, and the signature Dual Blade headlights. This is instantly recognizable as a Polestar , and it looks like it belongs both in the future and in an alternate reality (in like a safe version of Gotham City).
Also, notice how there's no longer a light bar at the rear? That's right, future Polestar models will come with these Single Blade rear lights which look way better. I'll go for split taillights over a light bar any day of the week. The latter just lacks character. By the way, the exterior color you're seeing here is brand new and it's called Nitrogen.
Photo: Polestar So basically, this is what you want from an EV , isn't it? To look futuristic in a healthy way, instead of a controversial way where you're trying to reinvent the wheel just for the sake of doing something different. German carmakers could stand to learn a thing or two from this recipe, Mercedes in particular.
"We wanted to evolve, while respecting, the core design values we demonstrated with previous models that define the Polestar brand in such a recognizable way. And with Formula 2030, with its clear Polestar design attributes like the Dual Blade headlights, wraparound visor-like windscreen and powerful haunches, we have done just that," said company design boss, Nahum Escobedo.
"But we've pushed perceptions, preconceptions and the expected as well, with our considered choices in form language, amplification of the performance topic and new detailing like the Single Blade rear lights."
Moving along to the interior, once you open those "opposing" doors, you'll immediately notice the pillarless design giving you easy access to the four seats. The cockpit itself appears to be somewhat driver-focused, and you get a 20" HyperDIM curved display mounted directly to the steering column. The 12.2" infotainment display is integrated into the center tunnel and you can lower it when you don't need it.
Photo: Polestar The driver can select between three modes in Performance, Normal and Autonomous. We needn't explain what they do. However, I will touch on that steering wheel design, because yokes are still controversial. This one, however, looks way more ergonomic than most - especially compared to what Tesla did on the Model S and Model X.
Polestar currently has five models in its lineup: The 2, 3, 4 coupe, 4 SUV, and the 5. Upcoming models include the 2's successor (2027), a 2028-bound Polestar 7 compact SUV, and the Polestar 6 roadster.

Dumped by Harley in King of the Baggers, Indian Challenges Honda, BMW, and Ducati to Join the Series
6 photos
Photo: Indian
Some seven years ago, America's two main motorcycle makers, Harley-Davidson and Indian, joined forces for a racing series unlike anything the world had seen before. Called King of the Baggers (KOTB), it called on touring motorcycles with bags attached to race for glory.
For almost seven years, the two companies took turns winning races and championships, and the relationship between them seemed unbreakable. Yet, not long ago, Harley-Davidson created another bagger racing series, one meant exclusively for its bikes: the Bagger World Cup .
Unlike King of the Baggers, Bagger World Cup is international, taking place alongside MotoGP races at various tracks. The inaugural season held this year, it seems, proved exciting enough for the Milwaukee brand to decide to exit KOTB and focus exclusively on its World Cup.
The decision was announced in early October, and it kind of took everyone by surprise, especially rival Indian, which saw itself left all by itself in the competition, and MotoAmerica, the driving force behind the series. The two have been scrambling ever since to keep the series going, and this week, it seems, a solution has been found.
Indian announced this week that it is backing no less than ten teams for the upcoming 2027 and 2028 KOTB seasons, through something called the ARO. That's short for American Racing Operations, and it represents a brand-new factory-supported team and rider program. This effort will be used to offer factory support at all levels, from bike transport and race maintenance to the tires the Indian Challenger motorcycles will use in the competition.
Indian will run ARO in partnership with long-time ally Vance & Hines Motorsports, and leaves the room open for individual sponsors to get in board. Moreover, the program also has a financial side that cannot be ignored.
Indian talks about more than $150,000 in contingency for teams and riders over a season, including a $20,000 bonus and a brand-new Indian Challenger two-wheeler for the season championship winners.
The ten teams that will be supported through ARO are not known yet, as the bike maker and MotoAmerica are only now inviting professional teams and riders to join. What is more exciting than that is the fact that now, left without a rival to fight against, Indian is looking elsewhere for competition.
Claiming that it wants to race against the best bagger bikes in the world, the American motorcycle maker challenged three other bike makers, Honda, BMW, and Ducati, to join the series.
The invitation is too fresh for the Japanese and European companies to have had time to think it over, but I am already tingling with excitement at the prospects of seeing the Challenger take on the Gold Wing, the R 18 (or K 1600), or whatever the Italians from Ducati can turn into something resembling an American-style bagger.

Maserati Doesn't Sell Many Automobiles; Maybe They'll Do Better With the Maserati Island in Dubai?
10 photos
Photo: Maserati
Maserati and Samana Collecta, an ultra-premium, lifestyle-focused real estate brand, recently announced the first residential living destination for the automotive marque with the trident. It’s naturally related to a marine environment, hence the name: Maserati Island.
Stellantis presented a brand-new business masterplan earlier this year called ‘FastLane 2030,’ and it covered 99% of its business case. One brand was left aside – Maserati, because the marque with the trident is getting its own dedicated business plan before the end of the year.
So far, all we know is that Maserati will reveal fresh concepts previewing the next-generation Levante crossover SUV and the Quattroporte passenger car sometime in December 2026, with the latter allegedly ready to give away its traditional sedan body style in favor of a shooting brake-inspired design. But the company is trying to cover all the basics, even though it doesn’t make too many cars.
For example, Maserati Classiche has recently certified a family-owned Maserati Ghibli SS , which is finished in fresh Giallo Fly paint over the original black cabin in a bid to properly celebrate the nameplate’s 60th anniversary. Also, Alfa Romeo and Maserati celebrate a year since they joined forces to create BOTTEGAFUORISERIE as “a new center of Italian automotive excellence.”
However, just in case you didn’t know, Maserati also likes lodging: earlier this month, the company said Maserati prepares to bring “its vision of Italian luxury to real estate and branded residences” with the new Casa Maserati label, which celebrates the 100th anniversary of the Trident by tapping into “one of the most significant trends in contemporary luxury: branded residences.” But wait, there is more.
Maserati promised that the “first projects and partners that will help bring this vision to life will soon be unveiled, opening up new horizons for the Trident,” and sure enough, they came up with a massive proposal: the Maserati Island! Together with Samana Developers and its new Samana Collecta brand, the luxury Italian automaker will operate the branded island as part of the Worlds Island complex in Dubai.
The Casa Maserati will express its vision on the Maserati Island with “sweeping Italian-inspired landscaping, leading to an architectural collection” that comprises no less than 840 branded residences. There will also be seven ultra-exclusive water villas and an additional couple of tree villas “nestled in lush greenery.”
Part one of the project includes 232 residences with private pools, including studios and one-, two-, three-, and four-bedroom configurations. All the residences will have “uninterrupted sea views, generous glazing, fluid spatial planning, and extended sightlines to mirror the sensation of being at the wheel of a grand tourer along the Italian landscape.”
"With Maserati Island, we’ve taken an important step in the journey that began with Casa Maserati, transforming our vision of Italian luxury into an exclusive living experience," says Santo Ficili, Alfa Romeo & Maserati CEO.
So, what do you think – yay or nay?

EICMA 2026 • MTPeak Stole Some of the Spotlight at EICMA 2026 With Insane Power and Retro Looks on Three Wheels
American Honda Pledges $3 Billion in Investments in the US Focused on Hybrids via Multiple Facilitie
6 photos
Photo: Honda
Honda recently said that it wants to "meet growing customer demand for hybrid vehicles in North America," so it's now building a brand-new auto plant in Central Ohio, among other things.
The Japanese automaker’s local subsidiary, American Honda , recently achieved its best October sales month in six years following a delivery jump of eight percent and stands at a five-percent growth rate after ten months and 1,269,213 total deliveries. The namesake Honda brand took the lion’s share, of course, rising more than nine percent in October and over five percent during the ten months to almost 1.155 million units.
Honda not long ago abandoned plans that almost came to fruition to bring new EV models built in-house to America, plus a collaboration with Sony for the Afeela brand, and took a massive hit across the ledgers. But they’re striving to get past that moment to refocus their business plans on hybrids, which are now seen as a better fit for North America.
The new plans will include the upcoming auto plant in Central Ohio, creating more than 2,000 new American jobs and increasing local production capacity to around 1.3 million vehicles annually. The new facility will be built alongside the existing Ohio manufacturing operations and is expected to start operations in 2029 (pending final government approvals). But the new factory isn’t coming alone.
It’s actually part of a broader set of investments that will positively impact the Honda operations in Ohio, Alabama, and Georgia, expanding and strengthening the integrated US production network to boost production and productivity of both HEVs and the engines and hybrid systems that power them.
"As Honda approaches 50 years of building products close to our customers in America, we are making one of the most significant commitments in our history to position Honda for the next 50 years,” said Bob Nelson, executive vice president of American Honda Motor Co., Inc. “These investments strengthen America’s role as a cornerstone of Honda’s global future and reflect our confidence in our more than 30,000 Honda associates and the strength of American manufacturing.”
Both Honda and Acura products will be covered by the new facilities, “including hybrid-electric vehicles and multiple new models currently under development by Honda R&D operations in the US.”
Back in May 2026, Honda revealed it will seek to introduce 15 new Honda and Acura hybrid models globally by 2030, with North America being the primary market for many of them. At the end of the investment road, Honda will have an integrated production capacity of around 1.3 million vehicles in the US and no less than 1.9 million in total across North America.
The investment numbers include the $3 billion for the new Ohio auto plant, 240k units in annual capacity for the new facility, a 250-percent increase in hybrid powertrain system capacity in Ohio, and 99% localized North American production for all Honda and Acura models purchased in the US back in 2025.

source_document.body:
Honda has been getting increasingly serious about electric motorcycles, but if you want to see just how weird the company thinks the future could get, take a look at the Honda EV Outlier Concept.
I got a chance to see the wild-looking machine in person at EICMA in Milan, where it looked like almost nothing else on the show floor. And that’s exactly the point.
The EV Outlier Concept originally debuted at last year’s Japan Mobility Show as Honda’s attempt to imagine an electric motorcycle that isn’t simply a conventional motorcycle with the engine swapped for a battery and motor. In fact, Honda describes the concept as looking toward the future of electric motorcycles beyond 2030.
The result is certainly unconventional.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
This ain’t your grandpa’s SuperCub .
Instead of a centrally mounted motor driving the rear wheel, the EV Outlier uses motors inside both wheels, giving it all-wheel drive and allowing Honda’s designers to completely rethink the rest of the motorcycle’s layout. The battery is housed in that large central black body, while the rider sits extremely low and behind it.
Honda describes the design philosophy with three words: “Gliding, Ecstasy, and Low.” The first refers to the smooth, nearly silent feeling of electric propulsion, while the second describes the instant acceleration and massive torque available from independently controlled front and rear motors. “Low” is more literal: Honda deliberately dropped the rider’s seating and eye position to create an entirely different sensation from a conventional motorcycle.
There’s even a bucket-style backrest designed to support the rider under hard acceleration and let the rider pivot through corners around their hips.
Up front, traditional mirrors are replaced by cameras, while a wide digital cockpit can display things like lean angle, riding modes, front motor torque adjustment, and what the two wheels are doing in real time.
Will Honda actually build this thing? Almost certainly not exactly as you see it here. That’s what concepts are for.
But the EV Outlier is still interesting as a statement of intent. Honda is obviously still playing around with the freedom that electric drivetrains offer, and the company is asking what motorcycles could become once designers no longer have to work around engines, fuel tanks, transmissions, and traditional drivetrains.
And judging by what I saw at EICMA, Honda’s answer could get pretty wild.

Time To Upgrade: Android Auto No Longer Works on Android 9 and Android 10
6 photos
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution/Google
Android 9, also known as Pie and released in August 2018, and Android 10, which received the green light for production devices in September 2019, can no longer run Android Auto. Google has updated the list of supported operating systems for the car projection system, so if your device is running any of these two versions, the only way to still have Android Auto behind the wheel is to upgrade your phone.
We’ve known for a while that this was coming. Notifications that new system requirements were coming started appearing on Android Auto for some users in October, and now it looks like the change has been silently implemented.
The system requirements listed by Google now point to Android 11 as the oldest version of the mobile operating system that can run Android Auto.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution The end of support Before you blame Google for leaving behind your ancient Android device, it’s important to know that moving to newer operating systems is required for new features and upgrades that wouldn’t otherwise be possible on old software.
With the migration towards AI everything, the switch isn’t necessarily surprising. Android Auto is getting deeper Gemini integration, with new features, such as Personal Intelligence, that will allow the AI-powered assistant to access data stored in other Google products, including Gmail and the Google Calendar, for personalized suggestions and answers.
As for how many devices are being impacted by this decision, the latest statistics shared in June 2026 show that 2.26% of devices were running Android 9, while Android 10 was still powering 4.1% of the Android devices worldwide. This means fewer than 1 in 10 Android devices out there are still running the dropped operating systems, so it’s safe to assume that not a lot of people will be affected.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution These numbers concern Android devices, not necessarily phones that are being used to run Android Auto. Android 9 received the last update on January 4, 2022, while the last update for Android 10 landed on February 9, 2023. Devices like Samsung Galaxy S9 and Galaxy Note 9 are, therefore, being left behind, as the latest OS version they received was Android 10.
The last time Google updated the system requirements was in 2024, when it dropped support for Android 8. Previously, Android 6 support was removed in 2022, so while many people expected only Android 9 to be left behind, Google is embracing a more aggressive approach and is dropping support for two operating system versions.
The new system requirements With this update, Android Auto needs at least Android 11 to run, no matter the connection method. The 2026 Android Auto wired system requirements mentioned Android 11 or higher and a high-quality USB cable.
These USB cables should allow for both data transfers and fast charging, as previously, finding the right cord for Android Auto was quite a challenge due to users unknowingly using charging-only cables to run the app.
You should always be using the cable that comes in the box with your phone.
If you want to use Android Auto with a wireless connection, assuming your head unit supports this connection method, you need at least Android 11 and “a compatible Android phone with an active data plan and 5 GHz Wi-Fi support.”
While these specifications could make you wonder if your device can run Android Auto wireless, there’s a good chance it can, as almost every new-generation smartphone meets these requirements.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution If your car is fitted with Android Auto wired but you want to use the app without a cable, your best choice is to use an Android Auto wireless adapter. Motorola MA1 and AAWireless are the most popular choices, as they connect to your phone using Bluetooth. They must be plugged into your Android Auto USB port in your car and then be in charge of receiving wireless data from your phone to forward it to your vehicle via the cable.
Just remember that running Android Auto without a cable can dramatically affect the battery life of your device. While this connection option would come in handy for short trips, such as when you go to pick up the kids from school, it’s not recommended to use Android Auto wireless without plugging in your smartphone on a longer journey. You could arrive at the destination with an empty battery.
Based on Google’s previous Android Auto system requirements update calendar, the next moment when such an update is supposed to take place is in 2028. At that point, support for at least Android 11 could be dropped, so be ready for an upgrade to a newer OS version or to get a new phone.
Google hasn’t released any announcement regarding the new system requirements, but considering the docs have already been updated, it’s safe to assume that the updated requirements are already in place, so your only option now is to upgrade your phone.

The list honors 50 life sciences employers of choice. Employees at SERB Pharmaceuticals and CSL Behring share why their companies stand out.
The BioSpace 2027 Best Places to Work list honoring exceptional life sciences employers that have U.S. operations features first-time and repeat winners in the large and small employer categories.
Bridgewater, New Jersey–based Amneal Pharmaceuticals ranked No. 1 among the 20 honorees with more than 1,000 employees. It’s the first time the company has claimed the top spot among large employers. Voters appreciated Amneal’s work culture encouraging innovation and growth.
Among the 30 honorees with less than 1,000 employees, Palo Alto, California–based BridgeBio came out on top. It’s the second consecutive year the company has ranked first among small employers. Voters highlighted BridgeBio’s commitment to patients and mission as well as its positive, collaborative culture.
Eli Lilly and Company , AbbVie, Legend Biotech and argenx rounded out the top five large employers behind Amneal. Tarsus Pharmaceuticals , Mirum , EyePoint and TG Therapeutics finished out the top five small employers after BridgeBio.
The Best Places to Work list is based on input from over 8,200 biopharma industry professionals. Nominations were in June, and voting took place through August. BioSpace received over 2,300 open-ended comments regarding what made nominated employers stand out.
Biopharma professionals rated employers based on several attributes: compensation; innovation; career growth opportunities; leadership; culture; diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI); reputation; and flexibility and remote work.
“Our 2027 Best Places to Work winners reflect biopharma’s ongoing commitment to thriving work cultures,” said BioSpace CEO Josh Goodwin. “These employers are making their employees feel supported and valued.”
To explore what makes this year’s honorees best places to work, BioSpace interviewed employees at SERB Pharmaceuticals and CSL Behring .
SERB Pharmaceuticals: Connecting people with the mission and each other
At Brussels-based SERB Pharmaceuticals, the Best Places to Work designation is a great recognition of the company’s culture, according to Marie Botin, SERB’s chief HR officer. The organization has a passion for helping patients facing rare diseases and medical emergencies, one that demands expertise, commitment and a willingness to work together, Botin told BioSpace . SERB employees, she said, not only possess those qualities but also see the connection between their contributions and the mission.
“This is really important because they understand where we are going, and they understand the impact of what they are doing every day,” Botin said.
Ali Kuhn, vice president of HR U.S. at SERB, also noted the tie between employees and the patients they impact.
“I think no matter what role you’re in at SERB, whether you’re a key account manager that has direct interface with hospitals and patients at times or in our roles in HR, we feel that impact through global communications, through patient stories, through really a lot of things here, so that’s really important,” she told BioSpace .
The Best Places to Work recognition is particularly meaningful at this stage of the company’s evolution, Botin said. Over the past 25 years, she noted, SERB has grown to more than 600 employees while keeping a culture of entrepreneurship, collaboration and teamwork across locations around the world.
One way the company unites its people is through an annual challenge in which global teams participate in activities such as walking, biking or horseback riding. While participants meet virtually during the challenge, the winning team spends a few days together in person and enjoys outings such as sporting events and theater productions.
In addition to the way people connect to the mission and each other, SERB’s benefits are another reason the company is a best place to work, according to Botin and Kuhn. In the U.S., Kuhn said, those benefits include affordable medical, dental and vision plans. Each year, she noted, SERB ensures that employee premiums are well below benchmark for companies of its size in the pharma industry.
Kuhn also highlighted paid parental leave, which SERB added as a U.S. benefit three years ago. The company provides 12 weeks of paid maternity leave for mothers and two weeks of paid paternity leave for fathers.
Another reason the company is a best place to work, according to Botin and Kuhn, is it offers many growth opportunities, which Kuhn highlights to prospective employees.
“When I describe in interviews what is the environment like, I describe an environment of agility and empowerment and accountability for not only you and your role, but for the global organization,” she said. “And I think that really speaks to individuals that are looking for a company like SERB at the size that we are, with the growth potential that we have.”
I think what is important is to make sure that we are keeping this culture fit—the same commitment, the same agility and the same entrepreneurial mindset.
Marie Botin, SERB Pharmaceuticals
Looking ahead at what can keep SERB a best place to work, Botin said the company is always considering what it can add but noted, “I think what is important is to make sure that we are keeping this culture fit—the same commitment, the same agility and the same entrepreneurial mindset.”
CSL Behring: Creating a culture that shapes the day-to-day experience
As someone involved in a workstream focused on his company’s employee experience, Jarrat Jordan has significant insight into what makes King of Prussia, Pennsylvania–based CSL Behring a best place to work. The research therapeutic area lead, immunology/transplant and vaccines, at CSL told BioSpace in an emailed response that during his first year with the organization, its strong sense of purpose quickly stood out. Jordan explained that the company has been helping people for more than a century, from its roots of protecting Australian communities against influenza and venomous bites to providing medicines for people with rare and serious diseases around the world today.
“There’s something powerful about being part of that legacy,” he said. “People are proud of the work we do and understand the impact it can have on patients and their families.”
Jordan also emphasized the importance of culture.
“A company can offer exciting roles, competitive compensation and opportunities for growth, but culture is what really shapes the day-to-day experience,” he said. “Creating an environment where talented people want to join, contribute and build their careers is incredibly important. Ultimately, it’s our people who enable our company to do what it does best: develop treatments that save and improve lives.”
Culture is especially critical in research, Jordan noted, as collaboration can be the spark behind a new idea or discovery.
“When people are engaged and willing to share ideas, challenge one another and go that extra step together, great things can happen,” he said.
In describing his employer’s culture, Jordan noted that while CSL is a large global company, it still has “a bit of that small and scrappy spirit.”
We have the resources and expertise to take on big challenges, combined with a real desire to be nimble and entrepreneurial,” he added. “To me, that’s a pretty special sweet spot.
Jarrat Jordan, CSL
“We have the resources and expertise to take on big challenges, combined with a real desire to be nimble and entrepreneurial,” he added. “To me, that’s a pretty special sweet spot.”
While he loves the culture, Jordan said what he likes most about working at CSL is probably the people.
“I have the opportunity to work with colleagues from all over the world, and there’s a sense of connection that can make it feel like an extended family,” he said. “Those different cultures, experiences and perspectives make the work more enjoyable, but they also bring new ways of thinking that can strengthen our science and innovation.”
This year alone, Jordan noted, he has traveled to Australia, Switzerland and China. He said that experience has been amazing and has made him appreciate even more what it means to be part of a truly global company.
As he considered what can keep CSL a best place to work moving forward, Jordan said he appreciates that the company isn’t standing still. It’s looking for practical ways to strengthen the employee experience and help people feel connected, engaged and empowered to do their best work, he said.
“For me, that’s what being a Best Place to Work is really about,” Jordan added. “It’s not simply earning a designation. It’s continuing to invest in your people and your culture and always looking for ways to be even better.”

Land Rover Celebrates the Colorful Diversity of Earth With New Range of Atlas Hues for the Defender
31 photos
Photo: Land Rover
The British specialty automaker Land Rover is taking special care of its most popular series, the Defender SUV, by introducing the new range of Atlas colors that celebrate the diversity of our home planet.
“The past, present and future of Defender inspire six new Atlas colors, for those who demand uncompromising quality and individuality,” says Land Rover, which has been making a return to off-road prowess with the series as of late. For example, they recently announced the global finalists who are now ready for an epic adventure in the inaugural Defender Trophy, a globetrotting event which marks the original British adventure brand’s return to global challenge events, no less than 45 years since the original concept was introduced.
They also recently introduced the Alasia pack in Europe , the Defender Dakar as an evolution of the Dakar Rally winner built for the road, or the cool Defender Vertex series, among other things. Even the Defender Classic had things to do, recently gaining a series of upgrades across the board and access to a V8 build to make it extra potent if anyone wants to.
Now, back to the Land Rover Defender Atlas, the new range of colors is said to be inspired by locations around the globe but also by the past, present and future of Defender. They’re also the first colors developed on the new Universal Paint Line facility at Nitra, Slovakia, after a recent investment in the European location.
“From the mountains of Australia to the wilderness of Africa and beyond, the new Atlas colors celebrate Defender’s exploration and adventure DNA,” says the company. Luckily, they’re not limited to certain models and instead are available across the entire lineup in a variety of specifications, including the new Defender Vertex, and the Atlas series includes six new shades spread across three categories.
Mara Red and Pantelleria Blue are inspired by the past, more precisely former Defender colors; Galway Green and Buckingham Blue are returning as heritage Defender paints, while Aira Green and Jenolan Gold are brand new options.
So, Mara Redis is a riff off he heritage Masai Red, Pantelleria Blue reimagines Pageant Blue, the Galway Green and Buckingham Blue are simply making a direct return from the heritage vault, while the new Aira Green and Jenolan Gold are inspired by “epic and breathtaking landscapes across the world.”
More precisely, Aira Green pays tribute to the Aira Force Waterfall in the Lake District, the United Kingdom, while Jenolan Gold is inspired by the limestone caves of Jenolan in Australia . The company says the new Universal Paint Line in Nitra, Slovakia, has “industry-first technologies to deliver precise color harmony,” using seven-axis overhead rail robots with automatically changing spray nozzles for “optimum electrostatic coverage and a flawless finish.”
The standard option for the new Atlas colors is a black contrast roof, and a white roof is optional, while the colors can be optioned from the factory with a Gloss or Matte Protective Film - Defender’s Protective Films also have “self-healing properties that use the sun’s UV rays to aid the repair of micro-scratches over time.”
The new shades add to the color palette of the Defender rather than replacing any of the old ones: the new Namib Orange introduced this year, Tasman Blue, Woolstone Green, and Carpathian Grey. The Defender X, Vertex, and OCTA models also have a Patagonia White Matte Wrap, with Fuji White as an option.
